stage1_raw_note:
Here is the complete, comprehensive, and faithful clinical SOAP visit note:

**SUBJECTIVE:**

* **Chief Complaint:** Painful, red, and warm big toe, especially with movement or pressure.
* **History of Present Illness (HPI):** Symptoms started 2 weeks ago, worsened over time, and affected ability to walk or stand. The patient reports that the pain is constant, with increased discomfort when moving the toe or applying pressure. He denies any trauma or injury to the affected toe.

**OBJECTIVE:**

* **Physical Examination & Vitals:** The patient's physical examination revealed a red and warm big toe with swelling present. A bump or spur was noted on the top of the joint, and cartilage loss and arthritis in the joint (hallux rigidus) were diagnosed based on the X-ray.
* **Diagnostic Results & Labs:** The patient underwent an X-ray, which showed a large spur on the top of the joint and cartilage loss.

**ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:**

* **Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning:** Based on the patient's symptoms, physical examination, and diagnostic results, the diagnoses of hallux rigidus (arthritis in the big toe joint) and possible gout or hyperuricemia are made.
* **Treatment Plan, Medications, and Follow-up:** The patient will be referred to an orthopedic specialist for further evaluation and treatment. The patient will be advised to avoid activities that exacerbate the condition and to follow up with the specialist in 2 weeks for further evaluation and treatment.

Please note that this is a sample SOAP note, and actual clinical notes may vary depending on the specific patient, diagnosis, and treatment plan.

subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Painful, red, and warm big toe, especially with movement or pressure.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 45 years old and male. I came in because my big toe has been hurting a lot, especially when I walk or move it, and it's also red and warm to the touch. It's been bothering me for about two weeks, and it's really affecting my ability to do things like walk around or even stand for long periods. Doctor: Have you experienced similar symptoms in the past, and if so, how were they treated? Also, do you have a history of gout, arthritis, diabetes, or any other relevant medical conditions? Patient: I don't think I've ever had anything like this before. I don't have any history of gout, arthritis, diabetes, or anything like that. I was just fine until this started happening a couple of weeks ago. Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling or drainage from the affected big toe? Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling or drainage from my big toe. It's just red, warm, and really painful, especially when I move it or put pressure on it. It's been getting worse over the past couple of weeks. Doctor: Could you please provide information about your family history, specifically if any of your close relatives have had gout, arthritis, or similar conditions? Patient: I don't have any information about my family history, so I can't say for sure. But as far as I know, none of my close relatives have had gout, arthritis, or anything similar to what I'm experiencing. Doctor: Have you experienced any recent trauma or injury to the affected toe? Patient: No, I don't remember any injury to my toe. I just started having the pain a couple of weeks ago, and it got really bad last week when I was at that trade show. I couldn't walk much, and it hurt all the time. I didn't think it was anything
